Expansive, awesome and beautiful. Fallout 3 is what RPGs aspire to.

Featuring a long absence from the 90s classics Fallout 1 and 2, Bethesda Softworks brings back Fallout for a new generation. Awaking in an apocalyptic nightmare, your own hope to survive in this new world is to explore, upgrade and befriend or back-stab as many people as you can.

Fallout 3 is a gorgeously realised game not only in its visuals, but the narrative, its atmosphere and the unremarkable but noticable human touches throughout.

Fallout 3 is one to recommend, albeit you can find yourself wandering through a carbon copy of the same underground tunnel or factory at times, but that's nothing to greatly disservice such a great experience.

In 2020 it's no longer a good idea to purchase this game. Even if you buy this game on Steam you will have a slow ass Windows Login after launching the game, which will extend the time it takes to launch this 11 year old game, and on top of that the game crashes every 10 minutes, and because you can't alt tab out of this shit game, you have to force shut off your whole system.

Fallout 3 is a wonderful game - certainly more than "Oblivion with guns". It's problem is that it can't make it past the big "now what?" moment. You finally reached level 20, beat the main quest, and when you ask yourself what to do next, there's not much. Once the world is explored, that's that. It could have been such a better game if Bethesda had implemented factions and small-time quests, like they did with Morrowind. In games like TES3, when you finished something, there was always something more to do - always. In Fallout 3, there is an end, and it seems to quick to come. Don't get me wrong, though. Fallout 3 is an immensely enjoyable game with a lot to offer to anybody who likes FPS or RPG games.

(Seriously though, this is my favorite game of the previous generation.)

This was the first game I played that I almost instantly fell in love with. at the time, not knowing a thing about PC gaming, I begged for an Xbox 360 to play it on so I wouldn't have to share with the rest of my family. My grandmother bought me one, and one of the first games I got for it was Fallout 3. At the time, I payed no attention to the bugs or errors that Bethesda made and only payed attention to the beauty of the Capital Wasteland. I most likey logged over 1000 hours on Fallout 3 on the Xbox 360, but sadly there is no way to check your hours. I do play the game on PC, but I use FOSE (Fallout Script Extender) and it disables Steam overlay. I started playing the game in late 2008 - early 2009 and din't stop playing it until the release of Fallout New Vegas. I have high expectations for Fallout 4, and I'm really hoping that Bethesda pulls through and gives us a game that will last me until the next Fallout comes.

compatibility on windows 10 is fine with a few quick tweaks to your FALLOUT.ini file (C:\Users\USER\Documents\My Games\Fallout3)

make these changes to the ini:

bUseThreadedAI=1
directly below the line you just edited add the line "iNumHWThreads=2" (without quotes of course)

for me this completely fixed crashing during gameplay

Fallout 3 was my July 2010. I would come home from work and play 5 hours, go to sleep, and repeat the process the next day. A solid month of quality storytelling, exploration, and an eerily beautiful nuclear landscape that I enjoyed every minute of. With my original copy, I bought the first 4 DLC packs at full price ($40) because I wanted to continue the experience. The GOTY version presents a staggeringly good value.

Had a pretty long ass review written on this but figured I'd shorten it up. This game is just as much the tits as it was 17 years ago. Graphically it's aged pretty damn well imo. Ive had zero issues and crashes, thanks to the removal of GFWL. Downloaded a couple of mods like the unofficial patch but honestly, it's a complete "plug-n-play" package right out the box; a rarity these days for games released pre-2010. Havent played it since before NV released and it was a breath of fresh air, with the bull shit that Bethesda has released since FO4 (havent played NV or 4 since their releases either for what it's worth). The music is solid and GNR (a radio station in game) is a must when playing the game. Overall it's still a fantastic game and rpg and holds up well in 2025. Just dont expect 2025 quality and youll have fun.

If youre like me and havent played 3 or any FO in awhile, it's definitely worth checking out or revisiting, especially if youre a fan of old Bethesda games.

Fallout 3 is an open world RPG Shooter with a first and third person perspective. It takes place in an alternate timeline which diverges from ours in about the 50’s. You are a Vault Dweller from Vault 111. At risk of spoiling you are compelled to track someone down and in and around the area of a destroyed Washington DC.

The good thing about Bethesda’s Fallout is that you are allowed to explore and play the game at your own pace. You are not restricted to time limits or anything like that. You can explore many ruins and even historic landmark buildings. There are several factions in the world you can ally with, or even destroy. There are tons of side-quests and unmarked quests that can keep you playing for a long time The main quest is short, but involving and the DLC is some of the best DLC around. Add on-top of that, the modding community has made many improvements to the game, and overhauls.

The downfalls are the shooter aspects of the game, some engine instability and its aging. However if you are not concerned with graphics then the rest isn’t a terrible concern considering the rest of the game.

I would definitely recommend this game if you enjoy Post-Apocalyptic games, or even the fallout universe.

This review isn't entirely about Fallout 3. To be honest, Fallout 3 was one of my favorite games of all time, even if it could be frustrating as hell at some points. I would honestly rate it right up there with Oblivion.

No, this is more about Steam's version of Fallout 3: GotY Edition and the terrible customer service. After playing the game on PS3, I decided to get it for my computer. It's capable of running Skyrim, not particularly well admittedly, but given Fallout 3's lower requirements, it should have been fine. However, after I finally managed to install the game with my crappy internet, I come across a disturbing piece of information. The game won't run. Oh, I can bring up the menu, but the moment I hit "Play", nothing happens.

I'll admit that I was aggravated, but I thought, "Surely I can just get a refund", only for Steam to refuse my refund simply because it wasn't even able to get the game installed before I had owned the game for two weeks. Even explaining that when I requested the refund just got me a refusal.

So with that in mind, I have a recommendation for you. Always be cautious before you buy any game off of Steam, especially if you have a poor internet connection like I do, since they apparently don't care about their customers at all.

tldr.text: Very Positive (81%): players love the story and characters, but bugs and crashes are the main complaint.
Mods and customization also earn praise.

details.text: Only 19% of recent reviews complain about bugs and crashes, against 32% of all reviews, though some say updates make the game "more buggy and unplayable".
Players with the least playtime are less positive than long-time players.
